title: Whitney Place rezoning and sign by-law changes
subtitle: Also covered: source water protection plan amendments and fewer restrictions on boulevard and real estate signs.
overview: The committee recommended a zoning change for 115-131 Whitney Place that goes further than staff proposed. Staff had suggested allowing only an expanded automotive use in the rear part of an existing building. The committee instead recommended allowing all general industrial uses across the whole building {{vote:m1}}. The change would not take effect until the Growing Together secondary plans by-law is in force.

The committee also recommended updates to the Sign By-law {{vote:m3}}. Special event directional signs could stay up all day, would need to show a date or day of the week, and the 30-day hold on removed signs would end. The changes respond to Council's direction to reduce boulevard sign clutter, and are proposed to take effect July 1, 2024.

The committee also recommended supporting technical amendments to the Grand River Source Protection Plan that apply in Kitchener {{vote:m2}}. These protect municipal drinking water sources. All three items go to Council for final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended, as amended, allowing all general industrial (M-2/EMP-2) uses across the whole existing building, rather than only an expanded automotive use as staff proposed.
The committee recommended that the amending by-law have no force and effect on the site until By-law 2024-064 (Growing Together Secondary Plans, Non-PMTSAs) is in full force and effect.
The committee recommended supporting the proposed technical amendments to the Grand River Source Protection Plan that apply within Kitchener.
The committee recommended repealing and replacing specific sections of Sign By-law 2011-099 and including the updated rules in the Municipal Code.

debate: A delegate for the property owner supported the staff recommendation but asked that all general industrial uses apply to the whole building. The delegate said the building already exists, no expansion is planned, and the flood line splits it along a straight line. The delegate also said a conservation authority planner had no objection.

Staff opposed allowing all general industrial uses. They said the no-cost expedited process is meant to legalize one existing use and involves no public circulation or neighbourhood meeting. Adding roughly 20 uses would normally be a major amendment with wider engagement.
A councillor asked whether neighbours had commented. Staff said the expedited process does not require circulation, so there had been no resident consultation.

On the Sign By-law, councillors said the changes would prevent boulevard sign clutter before it became common. They noted that some signs came from out-of-town businesses and welcomed ending the 30-day hold, which they said took up storage space and staff time.
Staff said the Sign By-law changes were minor and technical, and engagement feedback was generally positive. Real estate sign provisions were voted on separately because of a declared conflict.
